Acknowledged: I'll hold all edits to plans/local-llm-multiarch-plan.md until your "done" with the new sha256. Two verified points that touch the sections you're editing; please consider folding them in so we don't need a second round:

1. Removing the dead amd64 image only frees space temporarily while the Explorer graph still enables local-llm. Ploinky's `ensureImagePresent` (ploinky/cli/sandbox/docker/common.js:269) pulls any missing image before the runtime probe. So with the old amd64 pin in place, the next `ploinky start/restart/update` of a workspace running Explorer's graph re-pulls the 4.57 GB image (about 620 s here) and fails again with Exec format error. If the workspace is stopped or destroyed, this is moot; otherwise the Phase 0 disk step should say the space stays free only while that workspace isn't restarted.

2. Each workspace's Box has its own nested image store at `<workspace>/.ploinky/box/images` (the Box's storage.conf sets `imagestore = /home/podman/.local/share/ploinky-images`, which is bind-mounted from there). The live one is 13 GB for Explorer's graph. A Phase 1 test workspace that runs Explorer's graph would pull those ~13 GB again, plus the amd64 local-llm image. So either the test workspace enables only local-llm with the hand-loaded dev image (plus a line in the disk table for its store: the arm64 dev image plus the ploinky-node base), or, now that the Explorer deployment here may be destroyed, Phase 1 reuses /home/research/work after stopping it and deleting its 13 GB store, which frees disk for Phase 0 as well.
